headline: NEUTRAL
headline_tag: a month-long slide keeps Bitcoin under its 200-week line

action.title: HOLD at planned level
action.detail: Hold the planned budget level. The long-run uptrend still just counts, but Bitcoin is down about 14% in a week, about 11% under its 200-day average and 4% under its 200-week average, and a Rally watch drop window has been open since 11 November. Lead with trust and education, keep a reserve rather than raising spend, and only speed up after a close back above $72,859 (the 200-day average). If the headline turns BEARISH later this week, be ready to shift budget toward keeping existing users. This is a budget posture for planning, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC ($64,950) is about 11% under its 200-day average and 4% under the 200-week.
Down about 20% over 30 days and about 14% over 7; flat over 90.
26 days under the 50-day average ($79,341); Fear & Greed at 10 (extreme fear).
The 200-day average ($72,859) is still rising, about 6% over 90 days.
watch: The medium-term reading entered its weak zone today, and if it stays there five days in a row the headline turns BEARISH. A close back above $67,656 (the 200-week average) would ease that, while a close below $64,128 (the 30-day low) would make it more likely.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run picture still leans up, but only barely, while the last few weeks are clearly weak and the next month now leans down. Short term, the mood is in deep fear and price action is soft: at about $64,950 Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 26 days, sits about 18% below it and about 23% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 10. News is adding to the worry, as PANews reports about 13 EH/s of bitcoin mining power was hijacked and Luxor confirmed a breach of its mining-management tool. A normal week swings about $3,971, so a close above $67,656 (the 200-week average) would steady the week, a close below $64,128 (the 30-day low) would turn it clearly down, and in between it stays choppy; safety and explainer messaging fits far better than promotion.

The next month now leans down: the medium-term reading slipped into its weak zone today for the first time, and the headline only turns BEARISH after five days in a row there, which is why it still reads NEUTRAL. Price is about the same as 90 days ago, but the last 30 days are down about 20%; news is pulling this a little lower too, as PANews reports miner MARA sold 13,597 bitcoin in six weeks and Fed official Schmid says inflation is still too hot. Price must win back $79,341 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. Fed speeches this week, Nvidia's results on 17 November and the Fed meeting on 8 December are the scheduled events; keep bigger campaign pushes for after a clear turn.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up, but only just: the 200-day average is still rising (about 6% over 90 days), while price is about 11% under it and about 48% below its all-time high. The recovery is only back on track if Bitcoin closes above $72,859 (the 200-day average) again; $67,656 (the 200-week average) is the floor price is now about 4% under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. PANews reports Goldman Sachs, Citi and 19 other institutions are funding a joint dollar stablecoin for 2027, a small long-run positive, but more weeks below the 200-week average would weaken this picture clearly and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
